line_items.reasoning: Q2 adjusted EPS of $4.82 was strong enough to prompt a raise in FY26 adjusted EPS guidance to $17.80–$19.00 (midpoint ~$18.40) from the prior $17.20–$19.00 (midpoint ~$18.10), clearly exceeding the trajectory implied by prior guidance.
Consolidated revenue grew 7% YoY in Q2, above the 4%–6% full-year growth range guided last quarter, with U.S. domestic package revenue alone up 12% YoY.

FEC adjusted operating margin expanded 100 bps YoY (fifth consecutive quarter of expansion), directly contradicting the prior guidance of FEC margin being 'down slightly at midpoint'; however, FedEx Freight margin contracted ~300 bps YoY and the full-year Freight EBIT headwind was revised sharply from $100M to $300M, consistent with the guided Freight margin decline — netting to a beat on FEC but inline/miss on Freight.
No update to the $4.5B FY26 CapEx target was reported, and current results contain no indication of a deviation from that figure.
Voluntary pension cash contributions were further reduced to $275M, better than the already-lowered guidance of 'up to $400M,' reflecting improved capital discipline ahead of expectations.
